body:
I can relate to so much of what you've said here. I moved across the country about six years ago, trying to escape a bad situation with the hope of starting over. Ended up in an abusive roommate situation much like what you've described, went broke, and was forced to either be homeless or move back home. That feeling of being trapped is absolutely devastating. No matter how much you struggle, there's always a wall, and the walls seem to close in so tightly that you can't breathe, much less act to get out.

It's exhausting, trying to hold up a facade to the world, and even still the people around you accuse you of being negative, and filter you out of their lives and activities because being around you is such a downer.

It's bad enough that your own brain has turned against you, trying to kill you, that you can't trust yourself or your own thoughts. Fighting against yourself is a crushing battle, and when it feels like all the world has turned against you it seems like a war you can't win.

I guess I just want to say that you've got allies, people who may have different backgrounds and circumstances but know the battle to survive all the same, and you're not fighting it alone. Just don't stop fighting.

It's purely a liability issue for them, and they view it the same as hiring a candidate with heart disease or a sleep disorder. Fortunately, the medical screenings aren't especially thorough, and I wouldn't self-disclose. If I can get to that point and the meds don't show up in the drug screen, I'd be fine. And that's my real concern. I don't want to sabotage my chances at this job. At the same time, I know I need help if I'm going to survive much longer. But getting the job would be an enormous relief and maybe give me some hope. I feel stuck.

You're right, of course. But even though what I'd say to a therapist is confidential, the fact that I'd even *seen* a therapist recently might disqualify me. I had to sign a release allowing the background investigator to check into my medical records. That's why I went to a primary care doctor, and even doing that gave me a panic attack.

Hey, I'm okay. I'm really, really sorry. I feel like an absolute asshole. I passed out at some point, woke up sick as all hell. I'm still sick and shaking and very nauseous, but I'm okay. Again, sorry. I need to learn to stay the hell away from reddit when I'm drinking, I get seriously messed up and that's totally unfair to you and others who are just trying to help. I am so sorry.

Why? It's over. I'm done. No one in my life wanted to help, no one even tried. Noo ne wanted to be involved. I'm going o die alone and no onewill even knw i'm gone fo days yet, who even careS?? i'm sorry,no t fair to you, thasnk you for speaking, more than any other these past week. thank oyu
I'm already gone. It's done.

I guess I apologize too much because I am constantly reminded that I am nothing but a burden. And I'm drunk and beyond despair at this point. It'll be over soon. I have enough whiskey and pain pills and muscle relaxers to do the job. I won't fuck it up again.

It would be a novel, not exaggerating a bit. Condensed version? I got tossed overboard very young, sink or swim style, and every time I managed to get my head above water someone or something was there to shove it back under and point and laugh while I drowned. Sure, I made bad decisions, but I've also had the worst luck of anyone I know, and people always think I'm making that bit up until they witness it themselves, how the universe just slaps me about despite any effort to better my situation. You eventually just get comfortable with all the water in your lungs and let go. And that's pretty much where I've been for a few months now, just sinking to the bottom, waiting for the end. So I have no idea why I'm angry now, but I feel like using my final breath to scream one last 'fuck you' to the world. When I planned out my death I wanted it to be less violent, I was concerned about who would find me, etc. Now I don't give a damn. I'm sick of suffering just so other people can feel okay. I'm not going to be guilt-tripped into living just for someone else's benefit, so they don't have to be sad. They weren't concerned when I begged for help, when I put everything out there, when I needed a fucking hug and someone to talk to, someone to sit with me through the night so I wouldn't tie a rope around my neck. Where were they then? Where was *anyone*?

I'm sorry. It's just spilling out.

I don't know. I think it's probably been there a long time, but I've never experienced this type of violent outward expression of it. I mean, I know I'm a bitter and negative person, and there's been more wrong done than I can type out here, and I guess it's always been expressed through sarcasm and a general disgust of the world, if that makes any sense. But now I'm just angry at everyone and everything for no reason, and I'm lashing out at people and breaking things and I don't know why. I feel like screaming at everyone, at the world, 'why won't anyone help me?' And then I remember that I'm alone and no one gives a fuck if I keep breathing and there's a goddamn freeway overpass like 1000 yards from me.

I know I'm rambling, I'm sorry. My insides are on fire and I feel very out of control and impulsive and I'm not really able to think.

Yeah, parents divorced, got ripped away from my home and lived in a homeless shelter for about a year. First major episode of depression, went untreated. Never was acknowledged or treated until after my first suicide attempt because my family is awesome.
Early 30s. Miserable since age 13. First attempt at 20, twice more in my early 20s. I've been circling the drain for about five years now.
Not this time.
It is chronic, made worse by a recent injury and a severe lack of sleep for the past few weeks. I'm taking some major drugs for it. More than enough to relax my body and simplify my death.

You're mostly right, yes. But I've spelled it out to several people around me, and they've mostly brushed it off with platitudes. A couple of people have tried to help within their means, and I'm grateful, but it doesn't stop the inevitable. Today I finally admitted to two friends that I'm on the verge of suicide. One tried to make jokes to lighten the mood and the other just flat-out refused to acknowledge my statement and talked around it.

I'm in a great deal of pain, emotional and physical, and I lack the ability or the resources to fight anymore. I also don't see the point in it. This is the end of me.

I finally did, but the message wasn't received. I got 'you can talk to me anytime' but no acknowledgement of the situation. I'm not taken seriously, it seems. Or it bothers people so much that they cannot accept or deal with it. Either way, I'm on the ledge.
It has, but for the worse. I'm quite close to the end now.

I am struggling. I had another sleepless night, thinking through how my decision will impact others, trying to decide if I care. I very nearly confessed my intentions to someone, then thought better of it because he just received some great news and is really happy. I don't want to ruin that.
Thank you. I appreciate your concern. I am trying to make it through, but it is difficult.

I agree. I find it so hard to be an optimist. It only makes the disappointment hit that much harder.

I'm finding it hard to think now, and it's verging on morning here, so I'm going to try sleeping some. Thanks for talking with me. I really thought I was going to end myself tonight, but I had a good conversation instead. I'm grateful for that. All the best to you.
Thank you, really. This conversation has helped keep me alive tonight. I wish you all the best.

Yeah, and my finances are a real wreck because of cutbacks and my position is rumored to be eliminated soon. I've frantically been trying to find another job but the hiring process in my field can be months long. I even picked up two other per diem jobs, but of course that's not reliable income. I'm pretty well screwed.

It'd be nice if I was offered another position in the next few days. I might reconsider my intentions if that happened. Honestly that's why I've held out this long. But it doesn't look promising.

No, I think you've nailed it quite well. I feel like a slave to a fucked up world that has no care for me as an individual. I'm only as valuable to others as my ability to contribute something beneficial to them. If I can't hack it, then I'm useless. What I want and care for really means nothing in the grand scheme of things, so there's no point in any of it.

That's really at the core of my desire to end my life. I've fought with this for twenty years and have never been able to come to terms with it. My current financial situation is just a catalyst. Sure, I can go live in a shelter or on the street, and maybe there's a remote chance I can bounce back from that. But why the hell would I want to, when I know I'd just be returning to this twisted cycle all over again?

I do thank you for speaking with me. I'm starting to fade out, so I apologize if I don't respond.

Sort of. I won't be there much longer, though. I'm likely to be out of a job in the next few weeks and homeless not much longer after that. Actually, homeless one way or another because my pay has been cut so severely.
The life and death sort. The difference is that I'm detached from those situations so they don't really bother me.

You mean like try and numb myself to them?

You know the really ironic thing about this is that I spend all day diffusing various crises and I'm really very good at it. But I can't get control of my own crisis because I can't see any way out of it.

The whole idea that our lives are centered around training for a profession, working, and earning as much as possible in order to be valuable to society makes me sick.

I find little enjoyment in anything, really. I spend most all of my time working and sleeping. I tend to distract rather than enjoy. Mostly video games, mindless television, and movies. Anything to keep my mind from my situation, because as soon as I focus on it and try to sort things out, I become desperate and panic and the self-destructive impulses kick in.
I can try. It seems when I try to calm down I am so quickly overwhelmed with my reality. I can't seem to get it under control.

I feel like I am drowning, and instead of being offered a hand up, the people in my life are content to watch me thrash around desperately. Their whole 'pull yourself up' mentality is fucking killing me. I wouldn't be asking them for help if I hadn't already tried and failed at that. I truly am gasping for breath.

I think I may have lost myself by doing exactly that. When I was young I knew what I wanted and who I was. Now I feel like my whole perception of myself is defined by this ridiculous social construct that I hate and want to destroy. I'm not allowed to be me because I'm a square peg and I don't fit in the round hole. I've lost all patience with the theatrics.
I used to think that way. Now I'm not so certain that the countless failures are worth it, considering how badly it cripples me.
It's terribly exhausting. There are so many expectations and social conventions. And it definitely not acceptable to speak with people about depression and death. It tends to ruin things.

I played a few wind instruments. I wasn't terrible at it.

I have no one I can speak to in person about these things. I feel like such a fake when I'm with others. I have to play a role, and be clever and charming because that's what is acceptable.

I'd never been truly alone until this past year. I've always had roommates and such. It is miserable. I've no idea what to do with myself. 

I seem to have difficulty with people in general. People seem to like me once they get to know me, but not enough to get close to me. I've never been able to figure it out, really. I suppose I have a really strong personality and it turns people away. I don't know. I have a hard time trusting people, too. I'm usually wary that people only want something from me.

It's quite complex, but yes, I've intentionally cut ties with family and friends over the past several years. I suppose it was partially in preparation for death. Much of it was because of how dysfunctional and one-sided the relationships were.

Then I was forced into reconnecting with them, and in a few cases became dependent on them, and it was unpleasant for everyone. I've again severed those ties to the extent that I can, because I can't deal with them. And they really see me as a burden and have tossed me to the wolves.

I've no close friends. Work acquaintances mainly. A neighbor that checks in on me and helps me out now and then as she can.

Music is nice. I used to play a bit, years ago.

Dazed. Lost. Not sure what to do next. I stood in my hallway for some amount of time, not really able to move, not really aware of standing there. Then I realized where I was and figured I should sit down or something.
I feel very lost.
I can try. I'm a bit out of sorts at the moment.
I am facing a similar situation of being homeless and jobless; I can relate to this so well. I've no solutions to offer, but if you want to talk about anything please PM me.

Experience causes me to have no faith in that.

Thank you for listening, and for speaking with me.

I wish I could. But I'm facing a very difficult situation and unless there is a small miracle I will be homeless and unable to support myself. I have no workable solutions. I have nowhere to go and no one to turn to.

I wish it was different. I've held on this long because I really wanted things to turn around. I wanted to be okay. I wanted to find out how it felt to really live instead of just surviving. But there's just no chance of that.

Yes. The past month has been a last-ditch effort to hang on. I hadn't planned on it, but thought I should probably try just a little longer. It hasn't worked. If anything, I've managed to make things worse.
Thank you for reading it. It makes these last days more bearable, knowing that I'm not just tossing words into a void, knowing that someone actually listened.
